study type: Observational study comparing physiological responses to different postures
exposure: intermediate periods between main positions (spatial mobilization)
outcome: regional saturation of oxygen (rSO2) in the brain
cohort: Twenty stable mechanically ventilated preterm newborns were studied during the first 3 days after delivery.
finding: The four main postures (supine, right-side-lying, prone, and left-side-lying) did not show statistically significant changes in cerebral regional oxygen saturation, but significant differences were found during the intermediate period between right-side-lying and prone positions compared to other periods.
cross-section timing: During the first 3 days after delivery
